title: Your First Contribution
description: Ship it: turn audit findings into a scoped, submitted design contribution, and package it as a portfolio case study. Gate 4 — graduation.

objectives: Scope a contribution maintainers can accept: small, evidenced, respectful of project conventions
Write an evidence-backed proposal using the Playbook templates — titles as problems, open questions that invite critique
Navigate maintainer feedback: revise fast, defend once, and apply the silence protocol
Package your contribution as a five-section case study for your portfolio and Demo Day

resources.title: Your own Gate 3 audit
resources.desc: CORE RE-READ. Your evidence base. Re-read it before scoping is final: the finding you contribute against should be the one with the strongest evidence, not necessarily the one you find most interesting. They're usually the same; when they're not, evidence wins.

resources.title: The exemplary proposal threads (Contribution Playbook, Section 6)
resources.desc: CORE. You studied them in Lesson 7 for culture; re-read them now as templates for your own write-up. Note how each opener frames evidence in its first three sentences. Facilitator-maintained per cohort — see #contributions.

resources.title: Bitcoin Design Community — proposal discussion call recording
resources.desc: OPTIONAL VIDEO. Watch how a real proposal is received in conversation: the questions maintainers ask, the tone of pushback, how the proposer responds. Calibrates your expectations for what happens after you press submit. Facilitator posts the current pick in #week-9.

assignment.title: GATE 4: Contribution + case study
assignment.due: Contribution Friday · Case study Sunday · 23:59 WAT
assignment.submissionFormat: Issue/PR link + published case study + Demo Day presentation (slides by Wednesday rehearsal)
